sections.label: SEC. 516.
sections.heading: LAKE SIDNEY LANIER, GEORGIA, HOME PRESERVATION
sections.title: V

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Definitions
children.own_text: In this section, the following definitions apply:

children.heading: Easement prohibition
children.own_text: The term ``easement prohibition'' means the rights acquired by the United States in the flowage easements to prohibit structures for human habitation.

children.heading: Eligible property owner
children.own_text: The term ``eligible property owner'' means a person that owns a structure for human habitation that was constructed before January 1, 2000, and is located on fee land or in violation of the flowage easement.

children.heading: Fee land
children.own_text: The term ``fee land'' means the land acquired in fee title by the United States for the Lake.

children.heading: Flowage easement
children.own_text: The term ``flowage easement'' means an interest in land that the United States acquired that provides the right to flood, to the elevation of 1,085 feet above mean sea level (among other rights), land surrounding the Lake.

children.heading: Lake
children.own_text: The term ``Lake'' means the Lake Sidney Lanier, Georgia, project of the Corps of Engineers authorized by the first section of the Rivers and Harbors Act of July 24, 1946 (60 Stat. 635).

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Establishment of Program
children.own_text: Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish, and provide public notice of, a program--
to convey to eligible property owners the right to maintain existing structures for human habitation on fee land; or

to release eligible property owners from the easement prohibition as it applies to existing structures for human habitation on the flowage easements (if the floor elevation of the human habitation area is above the elevation of 1,085 feet above mean sea level).

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Regulations
children.own_text: To carry out subsection (b), the Secretary shall issue regulations that--
require the Corps of Engineers to suspend any activities to require eligible property owners to remove structures for human habitation that encroach on fee land or flowage easements;
provide that a person that owns a structure for human habitation on land adjacent to the Lake shall have a period of 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: to request that the Corps of Engineers resurvey the property of the person to determine if the person is an eligible property owner under this section; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: to pay the costs of the resurvey to the Secretary for deposit in the Corps of Engineers account in accordance with section 2695 of title 10, United States Code;

provide that when a determination is made, through a private survey or through a boundary line maintenance survey conducted by the Federal Government, that a structure for human habitation is located on the fee land or a flowage easement--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: the Corps of Engineers shall immediately notify the property owner by certified mail; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: the property owner shall have a period of 90 days from receipt of the notice in which to establish that the structure was constructed before January 1, 2000, and that the property owner is an eligible property owner under this section;

provide that any private survey shall be subject to review and approval by the Corps of Engineers to ensure that the private survey conforms to the boundary line established by the Federal Government;
require the Corps of Engineers to offer to an eligible property owner a conveyance or release that--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: on fee land, conveys by quitclaim deed the minimum land required to maintain the human habitation structure, reserving the right to flood to the elevation of 1,085 feet above mean sea level, if applicable;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: in a flowage easement, releases by quitclaim deed the easement prohibition;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: provides that--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: the existing structure shall not be extended further onto fee land or into the flowage easement; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: additional structures for human habitation shall not be placed on fee land or in a flowage easement; and

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: provides that--

children.label: (I)
children.own_text: the United States shall not be liable or responsible for damage to property or injury to persons caused by operation of the Lake; and

children.label: (II)
children.own_text: no claim to compensation shall accrue from the exercise of the flowage easement rights; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: the waiver described in clause (i) of any and all claims against the United States shall be a covenant running with the land and shall be binding on heirs, successors, assigns, and purchasers of the property subject to the waiver; and
provide that the eligible property owner shall--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: agree to an offer under paragraph (5) not later than 90 days after the offer is made by the Corps of Engineers; or

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: comply with the real property rights of the United States and remove the structure for human habitation and any other unauthorized real or personal property.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Option To Purchase Insurance
children.own_text: Nothing in this section precludes a property owner from purchasing flood insurance to which the property owner may be eligible.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Prior Encroachment Resolutions
children.own_text: Nothing in this section affects any resolution, before the date of enactment of this Act, of an encroachment at the Lake, whether the resolution was effected through sale, exchange, voluntary removal, or alteration or removal through litigation.

children.label: (f)
children.heading: Prior Real Property Rights
children.own_text: Nothing in this section--
takes away, diminishes, or eliminates any other real property rights acquired by the United States at the Lake; or

affects the ability of the United States to require the removal of any and all encroachments that are constructed or placed on United States real property or flowage easements at the Lake after December 31, 1999.

sections.label: SEC. 517.
sections.heading: BALLARD'S ISLAND, LA SALLE COUNTY, ILLINOIS
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: The Secretary may provide the non-Federal interest for the project for the improvement of the quality of the environment, Ballard's Island, La Salle County, Illinois, carried out under section 1135 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2309a), credit toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project for work performed by the non-Federal interest after July 1, 1999, if the Secretary determines that the work is integral to the project.

sections.label: SEC. 518.
sections.heading: LAKE MICHIGAN DIVERSION, ILLINOIS
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: Section 1142(b) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (42 U.S.C. 1962d-20 note; 100 Stat. 4253; 113 Stat. 339) is amended by inserting after ``2003'' the following: ``and $800,000 for each fiscal year beginning after September 30, 2003,''.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Illinois River Basin Defined
children.own_text: In this section, the term ``Illinois River basin'' means the Illinois River, Illinois, its backwaters, its side channels, and all tributaries, including their watersheds, draining into the Illinois River.

children.heading: Development
children.own_text: The Secretary shall develop, as expeditiously as practicable, a proposed comprehensive plan for the purpose of restoring, preserving, and protecting the Illinois River basin.

children.heading: Technologies and innovative approaches
children.own_text: The comprehensive plan shall provide for the development of new technologies and innovative approaches--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: to enhance the Illinois River as a vital transportation corridor;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: to improve water quality within the entire Illinois River basin;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: to restore, enhance, and preserve habitat for plants and wildlife; and

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: to increase economic opportunity for agriculture and business communities.

children.heading: Specific components
children.own_text: The comprehensive plan shall include such features as are necessary to provide for--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: the development and implementation of a program for sediment removal technology, sediment characterization, sediment transport, and beneficial uses of sediment;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: the development and implementation of a program for the planning, conservation, evaluation, and construction of measures for fish and wildlife habitat conservation and rehabilitation, and stabilization and enhancement of land and water resources in the basin;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: the development and implementation of a long- term resource monitoring program; and

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: the development and implementation of a computerized inventory and analysis system.

children.heading: Consultation
children.own_text: The comprehensive plan shall be developed by the Secretary in consultation with appropriate Federal agencies, the State of Illinois, and the Illinois River Coordinating Council.

children.heading: Report to congress
children.own_text: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall transmit to Congress a report containing the comprehensive plan.

children.heading: Additional studies and analyses
children.own_text: After transmission of a report under paragraph (5), the Secretary shall continue to conduct such studies and analyses related to the comprehensive plan as are necessary, consistent with this subsection.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: If the Secretary, in cooperation with appropriate Federal agencies and the State of Illinois, determines that a restoration project for the Illinois River basin will produce independent, immediate, and substantial restoration, preservation, and protection benefits, the Secretary shall proceed expeditiously with the implementation of the project.

children.heading: Authorization of appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out projects under this subsection $100,000,000 for fiscal years 2001 through 2004.

children.heading: Federal share
children.own_text: The Federal share of the cost of carrying out any project under this subsection shall not exceed $5,000,000.

children.heading: Water quality
children.own_text: In carrying out projects and activities under this section, the Secretary shall take into account the protection of water quality by considering applicable State water quality standards.

children.heading: Public participation
children.own_text: In developing the comprehensive plan under subsection (b) and carrying out projects under subsection (c), the Secretary shall implement procedures to facilitate public participation, including providing advance notice of meetings, providing adequate opportunity for public input and comment, maintaining appropriate records, and making a record of the proceedings of meetings available for public inspection.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Coordination
children.own_text: The Secretary shall integrate and coordinate projects and activities carried out under this section with ongoing Federal and State programs, projects, and activities, including the following:
Upper Mississippi River System-Environmental Management Program authorized under section 1103 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 652).
Upper Mississippi River Illinois Waterway System Study.
Kankakee River Basin General Investigation.
Peoria Riverfront Development General Investigation.
Illinois River Ecosystem Restoration General Investigation.
Conservation Reserve Program (and other farm programs of the Department of Agriculture).
Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (State) and Conservation 2000 Ecosystem Program of the Illinois Department of Natural Resources.
Conservation 2000 Conservation Practices Program and the Livestock Management Facilities Act administered by the Illinois Department of Agriculture.
National Buffer Initiative of the Natural Resources Conservation Service.
Nonpoint source grant program administered by the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Notwithstanding section 209 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962-2) or any other provision of law, in carrying out activities to restore, preserve, and protect the Illinois River basin under this section, the Secretary may determine that the activities--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: are justified by the environmental benefits derived by the Illinois River basin; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: shall not need further economic justification if the Secretary determines that the activities are cost- effective.

children.heading: Applicability
children.own_text: Paragraph (1) shall not apply to any separable element intended to produce benefits that are predominantly unrelated to the restoration, preservation, and protection of the Illinois River basin.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The non-Federal share of the cost of projects and activities carried out under this section shall be 35 percent.

children.heading: Operation, maintenance, rehabilitation, and replacement
children.own_text: The operation, maintenance, rehabilitation, and replacement of projects carried out under this section shall be a non-Federal responsibility.

children.heading: In-kind services
children.own_text: The Secretary may credit the value of in-kind services provided by the non-Federal interest for a project or activity carried out under this section toward not more than 80 percent of the non-Federal share of the cost of the project or activity. In-kind services shall include all State funds expended on programs and projects that accomplish the goals of this section, as determined by the Secretary. The programs and projects may include the Illinois River Conservation Reserve Program, the Illinois Conservation 2000 Program, the Open Lands Trust Fund, and other appropriate programs carried out in the Illinois River basin.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: Value of lands
children.own_text: If the Secretary determines that lands or interests in land acquired by a non- Federal interest, regardless of the date of acquisition, are integral to a project or activity carried out under this section, the Secretary may credit the value of the lands or interests in land toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project or activity. Such value shall be determined by the Secretary.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Work
children.own_text: If the Secretary determines that any work completed by a non-Federal interest, regardless of the date of completion, is integral to a project or activity carried out under this section, the Secretary may credit the value of the work toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project or activity. Such value shall be determined by the Secretary.

sections.label: SEC. 520.
sections.heading: KOONTZ LAKE, INDIANA
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: The Secretary shall provide the non-Federal interest for the project for aquatic ecosystem restoration, Koontz Lake, Indiana, carried out under section 206 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (33 U.S.C. 2330), credit toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project for the value of work performed by the non-Federal interest before the date of execution of the project cooperation agreement if the Secretary determines that the work is integral to the project.

sections.label: SEC. 521.
sections.heading: WEST VIEW SHORES, CECIL COUNTY, MARYLAND
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall carry out an investigation of the contamination of the well system in West View Shores, Cecil County, Maryland. If the Secretary determines that a disposal site for a Federal navigation project has contributed to the contamination of the well system, the Secretary may provide alternative water supplies, including replacement of wells.

sections.label: SEC. 522.
sections.heading: MUDDY RIVER, BROOKLINE AND BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out the project for flood damage reduction and environmental restoration, Muddy River, Brookline and Boston, Massachusetts, substantially in accordance with the plans, and subject to the conditions, described in the draft evaluation report of the New England District Engineer entitled ``Phase I Muddy River Master Plan'', dated June 2000.

sections.label: SEC. 523.
sections.heading: SOO LOCKS, SAULT STE. MARIE, MICHIGAN
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: The Secretary may not require a cargo vessel equipped with bow thrusters and friction winches that is transiting the Soo Locks in Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan, to provide more than 2 crew members to serve as line handlers on the pier of a lock, except in adverse weather conditions or if there is a mechanical failure on the vessel.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Inventory and Assessment of Other Dams
Inventory
children.own_text: The Secretary shall establish an inventory of dams constructed in the State of Minnesota by and using funds made available through the Works Progress Administration, the Works Projects Administration, and the Civilian Conservation Corps.

children.heading: Assessment of rehabilitation needs
children.own_text: In establishing the inventory required under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall assess the condition of the dams on the inventory and the need for rehabilitation or modification of the dams.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Report to Congress
children.own_text: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall transmit to Congress a report containing the inventory and assessment required by this section.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: If the Secretary determines that a dam referred to in subsection (a) presents an imminent and substantial risk to public safety, the Secretary may carry out measures to prevent or mitigate against that risk.

children.heading: Federal share
children.own_text: The Federal share of the cost of assistance provided under this subsection shall be 65 percent.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Coordination
children.own_text: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall coordinate with the appropriate State dam safety officials and the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $7,000,000.

sections.label: SEC. 525.
sections.heading: BRUCE F. VENTO UNIT OF THE BOUNDARY WATERS CANOE AREA WILDERNESS, MINNESOTA
sections.title: V

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Designation
children.own_text: The portion of the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness, Minnesota, that is situated north and east of the Gunflint Corridor and bounded by the United States border with Canada to the north shall be known and designated as the ``Bruce F. Vento Unit of the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness''.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Legal Reference
children.own_text: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the area referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the ``Bruce F. Vento Unit of the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness''.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Project Authorization
children.own_text: Section 541(a) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3777) is amended--
by striking ``implement'' and inserting ``conduct full scale demonstrations of''; and

by inserting before the period the following: ``, including technologies evaluated for the New York/New Jersey Harbor under section 405 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (33 U.S.C. 2239 note; 106 Stat. 4863)''.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: Section 541(b) of such Act is amended by striking ``$1,000,000'' and inserting ``$3,000,000''.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary, in cooperation with the State of Minnesota, shall design and construct the project for environmental restoration and recreation, Minneapolis, Minnesota, substantially in accordance with the plans described in the report entitled ``Feasibility Study for Mississippi Whitewater Park, Minneapolis, Minnesota'', prepared for the State of Minnesota Department of Natural Resources, dated June 30, 1999.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The non-Federal share of the cost of the project shall be 35 percent.

children.heading: Lands, easements, and rights-of-way
children.own_text: The non-Federal interest shall provide all lands, easements, rights-of-way, relocations, and dredged material disposal areas necessary for construction of the project and shall receive credit for the cost of providing such lands, easements, rights-of-way, relocations, and dredged material disposal areas toward the non- Federal share of the cost of the project.

children.heading: Operation, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, and replacement
children.own_text: The operation, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, and replacement of the project shall be a non- Federal responsibility.

children.heading: Credit for non-federal work
children.own_text: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project for work performed by the non-Federal interest before the date of execution of the project cooperation agreement if the Secretary determines that the work is integral to the project.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated $10,000,000 to carry out this section.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: In order to further the purposes of section 204 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (33 U.S.C. 2326) and section 206 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (33 U.S.C. 2330), the Secretary shall participate in restoration projects for critical coastal wetlands and coastal barrier islands in the State of Mississippi that will produce, consistent with existing Federal programs, projects, and activities, immediate and substantial restoration, preservation, and ecosystem protection benefits, including the beneficial use of dredged material if such use is a cost-effective means of disposal of such material.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Project Selection
children.own_text: The Secretary, in coordination with other Federal, tribal, State, and local agencies, may identify and implement projects described in subsection (a) after entering into an agreement with an appropriate non-Federal interest in accordance with this section.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Cost Sharing
children.own_text: Before implementing any project under this section, the Secretary shall enter into a binding agreement with the non-Federal interests. The agreement shall provide that the non-Federal responsibility for the project shall be as follows:
To acquire any lands, easements, rights-of-way, relocations, and dredged material disposal areas necessary for implementation of the project.
To hold and save harmless the United States free from claims or damages due to implementation of the project, except for the negligence of the Federal Government or its contractors.
To pay 35 percent of project costs.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Nonprofit Entity
children.own_text: For any project undertaken under this section, a non-Federal interest may include a nonprofit entity with the consent of the affected local government.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $10,000,000.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Definitions
children.own_text: In this section, the following definitions apply:

children.heading: Committee
children.own_text: The term ``Committee'' means the Las Vegas Wash Coordinating Committee.

children.heading: Plan
children.own_text: The term ``Plan'' means the Las Vegas Wash comprehensive adaptive management plan, developed by the Committee and dated January 20, 2000.

children.heading: Project
children.own_text: The term ``Project'' means the Las Vegas Wash wetlands restoration and Lake Mead improvement project and includes the programs, features, components, projects, and activities identified in the Plan.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary, in conjunction with the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, the Secretary of Agriculture, and the Secretary of the Interior and in partnership with the Committee, shall participate in the implementation of the Project at Las Vegas Wash and Lake Mead in accordance with the Plan.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The non-Federal interests shall pay 35 percent of the cost of any project carried out under this section.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Operation and maintenance
children.own_text: The non-Federal interests shall be responsible for all costs associated with operating, maintaining, replacing, repairing, and rehabilitating all projects carried out under this section.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Federal lands
children.own_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this subsection, the Federal share of the cost of a project carried out under this section on Federal lands shall be 100 percent, including the costs of operation and maintenance.

children.heading: Authorization of appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated $10,000,000 to carry out this section.

sections.label: SEC. 530.
sections.heading: URBANIZED PEAK FLOOD MANAGEMENT RESEARCH, NEW JERSEY
sections.title: V

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary shall develop and implement a research program to evaluate opportunities to manage peak flood flows in urbanized watersheds located in the State of New Jersey.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Scope of Research
children.own_text: The research program authorized by subsection (a) shall be accomplished through the New York District of the Corps of Engineers. The research shall include the following:
Identification of key factors in the development of an urbanized watershed that affect peak flows in the watershed and downstream.

Development of peak flow management models for 4 to 6 watersheds in urbanized areas with widely differing geology, shapes, and soil types that can be used to determine optimal flow reduction factors for individual watersheds.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Report to Congress
children.own_text: The Secretary shall evaluate policy changes in the planning process for flood damage reduction projects based on the results of the research under this section and transmit to Congress a report on such results not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $3,000,000.

sections.label: SEC. 531.
sections.heading: NEPPERHAN RIVER, YONKERS, NEW YORK
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: The Secretary shall provide technical assistance to the city of Yonkers, New York, in support of activities relating to the dredging of the Nepperhan River outlet, New York.

sections.label: SEC. 532.
sections.heading: UPPER MOHAWK RIVER BASIN, NEW YORK
sections.title: V

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary, in cooperation with the Secretary of Agriculture and the State of New York, shall conduct a study, develop a strategy, and implement a project to reduce flood damages and create wildlife habitat through wetlands restoration, soil and water conservation practices, nonstructural measures, and other appropriate means in the Upper Mohawk River Basin, at an estimated Federal cost of $10,000,000.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Implementation of Strategy
children.own_text: The Secretary shall implement the strategy under this section in cooperation with local landowners and local government. Projects to implement the strategy shall be designed to take advantage of ongoing or planned actions by other agencies, local municipalities, or nonprofit, nongovernmental organizations with expertise in wetlands restoration that would increase the effectiveness or decrease the overall cost of implementing recommended projects and may include the acquisition of wetlands, from willing sellers, that contribute to the Upper Mohawk River basin ecosystem.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Cooperation Agreements
children.own_text: In carrying out activities under this section, the Secretary shall enter into cooperation agreements to provide financial assistance to appropriate Federal, State, and local government agencies and appropriate nonprofit, nongovernmental organizations with expertise in wetland restoration, with the consent of the affected local government. Financial assistance provided may include activities for the implementation of wetlands restoration projects and soil and water conservation measures.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Non-Federal Share
children.own_text: The non-Federal share of the cost of activities carried out under this section shall be 35 percent and may be provided through in-kind services and materials.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Upper Mohawk River Basin Defined
children.own_text: In this section, the term ``Upper Mohawk River basin'' means the Mohawk River, its tributaries, and associated lands upstream of the confluence of the Mohawk River and Canajoharie Creek, and including Canajoharie Creek, New York.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: In order to assist the States of North Carolina and Ohio and local governments in mitigating damages resulting from a major disaster, the Secretary shall carry out flood damage reduction projects by protecting, clearing, and restoring channel dimensions (including removing accumulated snags and other debris)--
in eastern North Carolina, in--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: New River and tributaries;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: White Oak River and tributaries;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: Neuse River and tributaries; and

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: Pamlico River and tributaries; and
in Ohio, in--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: Symmes Creek;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: Duck Creek; and

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: Brush Creek.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Cost Share
children.own_text: The non-Federal interest for a project under this section shall--
pay 35 percent of the cost of the project; and
provide any lands, easements, rights-of-way, relocations, and material disposal areas necessary for implementation of the project.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Conditions
children.own_text: The Secretary may not reject a project based solely on a minimum amount of stream runoff.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Major Disaster Defined
children.own_text: In this section, the term ``major disaster'' means a major disaster declared under title IV of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5170 et seq.) before the date of enactment of this Act.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $6,000,000 for fiscal years 2001 through 2003.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary shall provide technical assistance to non-Federal interests for an evaluation of the structural integrity of the bulkhead system located along the Cuyahoga River in the vicinity of Cleveland, Ohio, at a total cost of $500,000.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Evaluation
children.own_text: The evaluation described in subsection (a) shall include design analysis, plans and specifications, and cost estimates for repair or replacement of the bulkhead system.

sections.label: SEC. 535.
sections.heading: CROWDER POINT, CROWDER, OKLAHOMA
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: At the request of the city of Crowder, Oklahoma, the Secretary shall enter into a long-term lease, not to exceed 99 years, with the city under which the city may develop, operate, and maintain as a public park all or a portion of approximately 260 acres of land known as Crowder Point on Lake Eufaula, Oklahoma. The lease shall include such terms and conditions as the Secretary determines are necessary to protect the interest of the United States and project purposes and shall be made without consideration to the United States.

sections.label: SEC. 536.
sections.heading: LOWER COLUMBIA RIVER AND TILLAMOOK BAY ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION, OREGON AND WASHINGTON
sections.title: V

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary shall conduct studies and ecosystem restoration projects for the lower Columbia River and Tillamook Bay estuaries, Oregon and Washington.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: In carrying out ecosystem restoration projects under this section, the Secretary shall use as a guide the Lower Columbia River estuary program's comprehensive conservation and management plan developed under section 320 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (33 U.S.C. 1330).

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Consultation
children.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out ecosystem restoration projects under this section for the lower Columbia River estuary in consultation with the Governors of the States of Oregon and Washington and the heads of appropriate Indian tribes, the Environmental Protection Agency, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service, the National Marine Fisheries Service, and the Forest Service.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: In carrying out ecosystem restoration projects under this section, the Secretary shall use as a guide the Tillamook Bay national estuary project's comprehensive conservation and management plan developed under section 320 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (33 U.S.C. 1330).

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Consultation
children.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out ecosystem restoration projects under this section for the Tillamook Bay estuary in consultation with the Governor of the State of Oregon and the heads of appropriate Indian tribes, the Environmental Protection Agency, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service, the National Marine Fisheries Service, and the Forest Service.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: In carrying out ecosystem restoration projects under this section, the Secretary shall undertake activities necessary to protect, monitor, and restore fish and wildlife habitat.

children.heading: Limitations
children.own_text: The Secretary may not carry out any activity under this section that adversely affects--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: the water-related needs of the lower Columbia River estuary or the Tillamook Bay estuary, including navigation, recreation, and water supply needs; or

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: private property rights.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Priority
children.own_text: In determining the priority of projects to be carried out under this section, the Secretary shall consult with the Implementation Committee of the Lower Columbia River Estuary Program and the Performance Partnership Council of the Tillamook Bay National Estuary Project, and shall consider the recommendations of such entities.

children.heading: Studies
children.own_text: Studies conducted under this section shall be subject to cost sharing in accordance with section 105 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2215).

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Non-Federal interests shall pay 35 percent of the cost of any ecosystem restoration project carried out under this section.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Items provided by non-federal interests
children.own_text: Non- Federal interests shall provide all land, easements, rights-of-way, dredged material disposal areas, and relocations necessary for ecosystem restoration projects to be carried out under this section. The value of such land, easements, rights-of-way, dredged material disposal areas, and relocations shall be credited toward the payment required under this paragraph.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: In-kind contributions
children.own_text: Not more than 50 percent of the non-Federal share required under this subsection may be satisfied by the provision of in-kind services.

children.heading: Operation and maintenance
children.own_text: Non-Federal interests shall be responsible for all costs associated with operating, maintaining, replacing, repairing, and rehabilitating all projects carried out under this section.

children.heading: Federal lands
children.own_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this subsection, the Federal share of the cost of a project carried out under this section on Federal lands shall be 100 percent, including costs of operation and maintenance.

children.label: (f)
children.heading: Definitions
children.own_text: In this section, the following definitions apply:

children.heading: Lower columbia river estuary
children.own_text: The term ``lower Columbia River estuary'' means those river reaches having navigation channels on the mainstem of the Columbia River in Oregon and Washington west of Bonneville Dam, and the tributaries of such reaches to the extent such tributaries are tidally influenced.

children.heading: Tillamook bay estuary
children.own_text: The term ``Tillamook Bay estuary'' means those waters of Tillamook Bay in Oregon and its tributaries that are tidally influenced.

children.label: (g)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $30,000,000.

sections.label: SEC. 537.
sections.heading: ACCESS IMPROVEMENTS, RAYSTOWN LAKE, PENNSYLVANIA
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania may transfer any unobligated funds made available to the Commonwealth for item number 1278 of the table contained in section 1602 of Public Law 105-178 (112 Stat. 305) to the Secretary for access improvements at the Raystown Lake project, Pennsylvania.

sections.label: SEC. 538.
sections.heading: UPPER SUSQUEHANNA RIVER BASIN, PENNSYLVANIA AND NEW YORK
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: Section 567 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3787-3788) is amended--

children.own_text:
by striking subsection (a)(2) and inserting the following:
``(2) The Susquehanna River watershed upstream of the Chemung River, New York, at an estimated Federal cost of $10,000,000.''; and

by striking subsections (c) and (d) and inserting the following:
``(c) Cooperation Agreements.--In conducting the study and developing the strategy under this section, the Secretary shall enter into cooperation agreements to provide financial assistance to appropriate Federal, State, and local government agencies and appropriate nonprofit, nongovernmental organizations with expertise in wetland restoration, with the consent of the affected local government. Financial assistance provided may include activities for the implementation of wetlands restoration projects and soil and water conservation measures.
``(d) Implementation of Strategy.--The Secretary shall undertake development and implementation of the strategy under this section in cooperation with local landowners and local government officials. Projects to implement the strategy shall be designed to take advantage of ongoing or planned actions by other agencies, local municipalities, or nonprofit, nongovernmental organizations with expertise in wetlands restoration that would increase the effectiveness or decrease the overall cost of implementing recommended projects and may include the acquisition of wetlands, from willing sellers, that contribute to the Upper Susquehanna River basin ecosystem.''.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall develop a plan for activities of the Corps of Engineers to support the restoration of the ecosystem of the Charleston Harbor estuary, South Carolina.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Cooperation
children.own_text: The Secretary shall develop the plan in cooperation with--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: the State of South Carolina; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: other affected Federal and non-Federal interests.

children.heading: Projects
children.own_text: The Secretary shall plan, design, and construct projects to support the restoration of the ecosystem of the Charleston Harbor estuary.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary shall develop a program to evaluate the success of the projects carried out under paragraph (2) in meeting ecosystem restoration goals.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Studies
children.own_text: Evaluations under subparagraph (A) shall be conducted in consultation with the appropriate Federal, State, and local agencies.

children.heading: Development of plan
children.own_text: The Federal share of the cost of development of the plan under subsection (a)(1) shall be 65 percent.

children.heading: Project planning, design, construction, and evaluation
children.own_text: The Federal share of the cost of planning, design, construction, and evaluation of a project under paragraphs (2) and (3) of subsection (a) shall be 65 percent.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: Credit for land, easements, and rights-of-way
children.own_text: The Secretary shall credit the non-Federal interest for the value of any land, easement, right-of-way, dredged material disposal area, or relocation provided for carrying out a project under subsection (a)(2).

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Form
children.own_text: The non-Federal interest may provide up to 50 percent of the non-Federal share in the form of services, materials, supplies, or other in-kind contributions.

children.heading: Operation and maintenance
children.own_text: The operation, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, and replacement of projects carried out under this section shall be a non-Federal responsibility.

children.heading: Non-federal interests
children.own_text: Notwithstanding section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d-5b), for any project carried out under this section, a non-Federal interest may include a private interest and a nonprofit entity.

children.heading: Development of plan
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out subsection (a)(1) $300,000.

children.heading: Other activities
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out paragraphs (2) and (3) of subsection (a) $5,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2001 through 2004.

sections.label: SEC. 542.
sections.heading: LAKE CHAMPLAIN WATERSHED, VERMONT AND NEW YORK
sections.title: V

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Definitions
children.own_text: In this section, the following definitions apply:

children.heading: Critical restoration project
children.own_text: The term ``critical restoration project'' means a project that will produce, consistent with Federal programs, projects, and activities, immediate and substantial ecosystem restoration, preservation, and protection benefits.

children.heading: Lake champlain watershed
children.own_text: The term ``Lake Champlain watershed'' means--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: the land areas within Addison, Bennington, Caledonia, Chittenden, Franklin, Grand Isle, Lamoille, Orange, Orleans, Rutland, and Washington Counties in the State of Vermont; and

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: the land areas that drain into Lake Champlain and that are located within Essex, Clinton, Franklin, Warren, and Washington Counties in the State of New York; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: the near-shore areas of Lake Champlain within the counties referred to in clause (i).

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary may participate in critical restoration projects in the Lake Champlain watershed.

children.heading: Types of projects
children.own_text: A critical restoration project shall be eligible for assistance under this section if the critical restoration project consists of--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: implementation of an intergovernmental agreement for coordinating regulatory and management responsibilities with respect to the Lake Champlain watershed;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: acceleration of whole farm planning to implement best management practices to maintain or enhance water quality and to promote agricultural land use in the Lake Champlain watershed;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: acceleration of whole community planning to promote intergovernmental cooperation in the regulation and management of activities consistent with the goal of maintaining or enhancing water quality in the Lake Champlain watershed;

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: natural resource stewardship activities on public or private land to promote land uses that--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: preserve and enhance the economic and social character of the communities in the Lake Champlain watershed; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: protect and enhance water quality; or

children.label: (E)
children.own_text: any other activity determined by the Secretary to be appropriate.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Public Ownership Requirement
children.own_text: The Secretary may provide assistance for a critical restoration project under this section only if--
the critical restoration project is publicly owned; or

the non-Federal interest with respect to the critical restoration project demonstrates that the critical restoration project will provide a substantial public benefit in the form of water quality improvement.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: In consultation with the Lake Champlain Basin Program and the heads of other appropriate Federal, State, tribal, and local agencies, the Secretary may--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: identify critical restoration projects in the Lake Champlain watershed; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: carry out the critical restoration projects after entering into an agreement with an appropriate non-Federal interest in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d-5b) and this section.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: A critical restoration project shall be eligible for financial assistance under this section only if the appropriate State official for the critical restoration project certifies to the Secretary that the critical restoration project will contribute to the protection and enhancement of the quality or quantity of the water resources of the Lake Champlain watershed.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Special consideration
children.own_text: In certifying critical restoration projects to the Secretary, the appropriate State officials shall give special consideration to projects that implement plans, agreements, and measures that preserve and enhance the economic and social character of the communities in the Lake Champlain watershed.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Before providing assistance under this section with respect to a critical restoration project, the Secretary shall enter into a project cooperation agreement that shall require the non-Federal interest--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: to pay 35 percent of the total costs of the project;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: to provide any land, easements, rights-of-way, dredged material disposal areas, and relocations necessary to carry out the project;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: to pay 100 percent of the operation, maintenance, repair, replacement, and rehabilitation costs associated with the project; and

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: to hold the United States harmless from any claim or damage that may arise from carrying out the project, except any claim or damage that may arise from the negligence of the Federal Government or a contractor of the Federal Government.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: Credit for design work
children.own_text: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for the reasonable costs of design work carried out by the non-Federal interest before the date of execution of a project cooperation agreement for the critical restoration project, if the Secretary finds that the design work is integral to the project.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Credit for land, easements, and rights-of-way
children.own_text: The Secretary shall credit the non-Federal interest for the value of any land, easement, right-of-way, dredged material disposal area, or relocation provided for carrying out the project.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Form
children.own_text: The non-Federal interest may provide up to 50 percent of the non-Federal share in the form of services, materials, supplies, or other in-kind contributions.

children.label: (f)
children.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws
children.own_text: Nothing in this section waives, limits, or otherwise affects the applicability of Federal or State law with respect to a project carried out with assistance provided under this section.

children.label: (g)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $20,000,000, to remain available until expended.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary--
shall conduct a study to evaluate the structural integrity and need for modification or removal of each dam located in the State of Vermont and described in subsection (b);
shall provide to the non-Federal interest design analysis, plans and specifications, and cost estimates for repair, restoration, modification, and removal of each dam described in subsection (b); and
may carry out measures to prevent or mitigate against such risk if the Secretary determines that a dam described in subsection (b) presents an imminent and substantial risk to public safety.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Dams To Be Evaluated
children.own_text: The dams referred to in subsection (a) are the following:
East Barre Dam, Barre Town.
Wrightsville Dam, Middlesex-Montpelier.
Lake Sadawga Dam, Whitingham.
Dufresne Pond Dam, Manchester.
Knapp Brook Site 1 Dam, Cavendish.
Lake Bomoseen Dam, Castleton.
Little Hosmer Dam, Craftsbury.
Colby Pond Dam, Plymouth.
Silver Lake Dam, Barnard.
Gale Meadows Dam, Londonderry.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Cost Sharing
children.own_text: The non-Federal share of the cost of activities under subsection (a) shall be 35 percent.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Coordination
children.own_text: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall coordinate with the appropriate State dam safety officials and the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $5,000,000.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Definition of Critical Restoration Project
children.own_text: In this section, the term ``critical restoration project'' means a project that will produce, consistent with Federal programs, projects, and activities, immediate and substantial ecosystem restoration, preservation, and protection benefits.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Critical Restoration Projects
children.own_text: The Secretary may participate in critical restoration projects in the area of Puget Sound, Washington, and adjacent waters, including--

Hood Canal;
Rosario Strait; and
the Strait of Juan de Fuca to Cape Flattery.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary may identify critical restoration projects in the area described in subsection (b) based on--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: studies to determine the feasibility of carrying out the critical restoration projects; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: analyses conducted before the date of enactment of this Act by non-Federal interests.

children.heading: Criteria and procedures for review and approval

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: In consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of the Interior, the Governor of the State of Washington, tribal governments, and the heads of other appropriate Federal, State, and local agencies, the Secretary may develop criteria and procedures for prioritizing projects identified under paragraph (1).

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Consistency with fish restoration goals
children.own_text: The criteria and procedures developed under subparagraph (A) shall be consistent with fish restoration goals of the National Marine Fisheries Service and the State of Washington.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Use of existing studies and plans
children.own_text: In carrying out subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall use, to the maximum extent practicable, studies and plans in existence on the date of enactment of this Act to identify project needs and priorities.

children.heading: Local participation
children.own_text: In prioritizing projects for implementation under this section, the Secretary shall consult with, and consider the priorities of, public and private entities that are active in watershed planning and ecosystem restoration in Puget Sound watersheds, including--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: the Salmon Recovery Funding Board;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: the Northwest Straits Commission;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: the Hood Canal Coordinating Council;

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: county watershed planning councils; and

children.label: (E)
children.own_text: salmon enhancement groups.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Implementation
children.own_text: The Secretary may carry out projects identified under subsection (c) after entering into an agreement with an appropriate non-Federal interest in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d-5b) and this section.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Before carrying out any project under this section, the Secretary shall enter into a binding agreement with the non-Federal interest that shall require the non-Federal interest--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: to pay 35 percent of the total costs of the project;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: to provide any land, easements, rights-of-way, dredged material disposal areas and relocations necessary to carry out the project;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: to pay 100 percent of the operation, maintenance, repair, replacement, and rehabilitation costs associated with the project; and

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: to hold the United States harmless from any claim or damage that may arise from carrying out the project, except any claim or damage that may arise from the negligence of the Federal Government or a contractor of the Federal Government.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary shall credit the non- Federal interest for the value of any land, easement, right-of-way, dredged material disposal area, or relocation provided for carrying out the project.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Form
children.own_text: The non-Federal interest may provide up to 50 percent of the non-Federal share in the form of services, materials, supplies, or other in-kind contributions.

children.label: (f)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $40,000,000, of which not more than $5,000,000 may be used to carry out any 1 critical restoration project.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Study
children.own_text: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the feasibility of providing coastal erosion protection for the tribal reservation of the Shoalwater Bay Tribe on Willapa Bay, Washington.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of law (including any requirement for economic justification), the Secretary may construct and maintain a project to provide coastal erosion protection for the tribal reservation of the Shoalwater Bay Tribe on Willapa Bay, Washington, at Federal expense, if the Secretary determines that the project--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: is a cost-effective means of providing erosion protection;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: is environmentally acceptable and technically feasible; and

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: will improve the economic and social conditions of the Shoalwater Bay Tribe.

children.heading: Land, easements, and rights-of-way
children.own_text: As a condition of the project described in paragraph (1), the Shoalwater Bay Tribe shall provide lands, easements, rights-of-way, and dredged material disposal areas necessary for implementation of the project.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The city of Aberdeen, Washington, may transfer all rights, title, and interests of the city in the land transferred to the city under section 203 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1990 (104 Stat. 4632) to the city of Tacoma, Washington.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Conditions
children.own_text: The transfer under this section shall be subject to the conditions set forth in section 203(b) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1990 (104 Stat. 4632); except that the condition set forth in paragraph (1) of such section shall apply to the city of Tacoma only for so long as the city of Tacoma has a valid license with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission relating to operation of the Wynoochee Dam, Washington.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Limitation
children.own_text: The transfer under subsection (a) may be made only after the Secretary determines that the city of Tacoma will be able to operate, maintain, repair, replace, and rehabilitate the project for Wynoochee Lake, Wynoochee River, Washington, authorized by section 203 of the Flood Control Act of 1962 (76 Stat. 1193), in accordance with such regulations as the Secretary may issue to ensure that such operation, maintenance, repair, replacement, and rehabilitation is consistent with project purposes.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Water Supply Contract
children.own_text: The water supply contract designated as DACWD 67-68-C-0024 shall be null and void if the Secretary exercises the reversionary right set forth in section 203(b)(3) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1990 (104 Stat. 4632).

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The project for flood control, Bluestone Lake, Ohio River basin, West Virginia, authorized by section 4 of the Flood Control Act of June 28, 1938 (52 Stat. 1217), is modified to authorize construction of hydroelectric generating facilities at the project by the Tri-Cities Power Authority of West Virginia under the terms and conditions of the agreement referred to in subsection (b).

children.heading: Agreement terms
children.own_text: The Secretary and the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Southeastern Power Administration, shall enter into a binding agreement with the Tri-Cities Power Authority that contains mutually acceptable terms and conditions and under which the Tri-Cities Power Authority agrees to each of the following:

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: To design and construct the generating facilities referred to in subsection (a) within 4 years after the date of such agreement.

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: To reimburse the Secretary for--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: the cost of approving such design and inspecting such construction;

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: the cost of providing any assistance authorized under subsection (c)(2); and

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: the redistributed costs associated with the original construction of the dam and dam safety if all parties agree with the method of the development of the chargeable amounts associated with hydropower at the facility.

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: To release and indemnify the United States from any claims, causes of action, or liabilities that may arise from such design and construction of the facilities referred to in subsection (a), including any liability that may arise out of the removal of the facility if directed by the Secretary.

children.heading: Additional terms
children.own_text: The agreement shall also specify each of the following:

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: The procedures and requirements for approval and acceptance of design, construction, and operation and maintenance of the facilities referred to in subsection (a).

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: The rights, responsibilities, and liabilities of each party to the agreement.

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: The amount of the payments under subsection (f) and the procedures under which such payments are to be made.

children.heading: Prohibition
children.own_text: No Federal funds may be expended for the design, construction, and operation and maintenance of the facilities referred to in subsection (a) prior to the date on which such facilities are accepted by the Secretary under subsection (d).

children.heading: Reimbursement
children.own_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, if requested by the Tri-Cities Power Authority, the Secretary may provide, on a reimbursable basis, assistance in connection with the design and construction of the generating facilities referred to in subsection (a).

children.heading: Transfer of facilities
children.own_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, upon completion of the construction of the facilities referred to in subsection (a) and final approval of such facilities by the Secretary, the Tri-Cities Power Authority shall transfer without consideration title to such facilities to the United States, and the Secretary shall--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: accept the transfer of title to such facilities on behalf of the United States; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: operate and maintain the facilities.

children.heading: Certification
children.own_text: The Secretary may accept title to the facilities pursuant to paragraph (1) only after certifying that the quality of the construction meets all standards established for similar facilities constructed by the Secretary.

children.heading: Authorized project purposes
children.own_text: The operation and maintenance of the facilities shall be conducted in a manner that is consistent with other authorized project purposes of the Bluestone Lake facility.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Excess Power
children.own_text: Pursuant to any agreement under subsection (b), the Southeastern Power Administration shall market the excess power produced by the facilities referred to in subsection (a) in accordance with section 5 of the Rivers and Harbors Act of December 22, 1944 (16 U.S.C. 825s; 58 Stat. 890).

children.label: (f)
children.heading: Payments
children.own_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Southeastern Power Administration, may pay, in accordance with the terms of the agreement entered into under subsection (b), out of the revenues from the sale of power produced by the generating facility of the interconnected systems of reservoirs operated by the Secretary and marketed by the Southeastern Power Administration--

to the Tri-Cities Power Authority all reasonable costs incurred by the Tri-Cities Power Authority in the design and construction of the facilities referred to in subsection (a), including the capital investment in such facilities and a reasonable rate of return on such capital investment; and

to the Secretary, in accordance with the terms of the agreement entered into under subsection (b) out of the revenues from the sale of power produced by the generating facility of the interconnected systems of reservoirs operated by the Secretary and marketed by the Southeastern Power Administration, all reasonable costs incurred by the Secretary in the operation and maintenance of facilities referred to in subsection (a).

children.label: (g)
children.heading: Authority of Secretary of Energy
children.own_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Southeastern Power Administration, is authorized--
to construct such transmission facilities as necessary to market the power produced at the facilities referred to in subsection (a) with funds contributed by the Tri-Cities Power Authority; and

to repay those funds, including interest and any administrative expenses, directly from the revenues from the sale of power produced by such facilities of the interconnected systems of reservoirs operated by the Secretary and marketed by the Southeastern Power Administration.

children.label: (h)
children.heading: Savings Clause
children.own_text: Nothing in this section affects any requirement under Federal or State environmental law relating to the licensing or operation of the facilities referred to in subsection (a).

sections.label: SEC. 548.
sections.heading: LESAGE/GREENBOTTOM SWAMP, WEST VIRGINIA

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary may provide planning and design assistance to non-Federal interests for projects located along the Tug Fork River in West Virginia and identified by the master plan developed pursuant to section 114(t) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (106 Stat. 4820).

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Priorities
children.own_text: In providing assistance under this section, the Secretary shall give priority to the primary development demonstration sites in West Virginia identified by the master plan referred to in subsection (a).

children.label: (c)

sections.label: SEC. 554.
sections.heading: HYDROGRAPHIC SURVEY
sections.title: V
sections.own_text: The Secretary shall enter into an agreement with the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration--

children.own_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Tennessee Valley Authority shall grant a release or releases, without monetary consideration, from the restrictive covenant that requires that property described in subsection (b) shall at all times be used solely for the purpose of erecting docks and buildings for shipbuilding purposes or for the manufacture or storage of products for the purpose of trading or shipping in transportation.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Definitions
children.own_text: In this section, the following definitions apply:

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The term ``Central and Southern Florida Project'' means the project for Central and Southern Florida authorized under the heading ``central and southern florida'' in section 203 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 (62 Stat. 1176).

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Inclusion
children.own_text: The term ``Central and Southern Florida Project'' includes any modification to the project authorized by this section or any other provision of law.

children.heading: Governor
children.own_text: The term ``Governor'' means the Governor of the State of Florida.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The term ``natural system'' means all land and water managed by the Federal Government or the State within the South Florida ecosystem.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Inclusions
children.own_text: The term ``natural system'' includes--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: water conservation areas;

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: sovereign submerged land;

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: Everglades National Park;

children.label: (iv)
children.own_text: Biscayne National Park;

children.label: (v)
children.own_text: Big Cypress National Preserve;

children.label: (vi)
children.own_text: other Federal or State (including a political subdivision of a State) land that is designated and managed for conservation purposes; and

children.label: (vii)
children.own_text: any tribal land that is designated and managed for conservation purposes, as approved by the tribe.

children.heading: Plan
children.own_text: The term ``Plan'' means the Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan contained in the ``Final Integrated Feasibility Report and Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement'', dated April 1, 1999, as modified by this section.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The term ``South Florida ecosystem'' means the area consisting of the land and water within the boundary of the South Florida Water Management District in effect on July 1, 1999.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Inclusions
children.own_text: The term ``South Florida ecosystem'' includes--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: the Everglades;

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: the Florida Keys; and

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: the contiguous near-shore coastal water of South Florida.

children.heading: State
children.own_text: The term ``State'' means the State of Florida.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Except as modified by this section, the Plan is approved as a framework for modifications and operational changes to the Central and Southern Florida Project that are needed to restore, preserve, and protect the South Florida ecosystem while providing for other water-related needs of the region, including water supply and flood protection. The Plan shall be implemented to ensure the protection of water quality in, the reduction of the loss of fresh water from, and the improvement of the environment of the South Florida ecosystem and to achieve and maintain the benefits to the natural system and human environment described in the Plan, and required pursuant to this section, for as long as the project is authorized.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Integration
children.own_text: In carrying out the Plan, the Secretary shall integrate the activities described in subparagraph (A) with ongoing Federal and State projects and activities in accordance with section 528(c) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3769). Unless specifically provided herein, nothing in this section shall be construed to modify any existing cost share or responsibility for projects as listed in subsection (c) or (e) of section 528 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3769).

children.label: (i)
children.heading: Projects
children.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out the projects included in the Plan in accordance with subparagraphs (B), (C), (D), and (E).

children.label: (ii)
children.heading: Considerations
children.own_text: In carrying out activities described in the Plan, the Secretary shall--

children.label: (I)
children.own_text: take into account the protection of water quality by considering applicable State water quality standards; and

children.label: (II)
children.own_text: include such features as the Secretary determines are necessary to ensure that all ground water and surface water discharges from any project feature authorized by this subsection will meet all applicable water quality standards and applicable water quality permitting requirements.

children.label: (iii)
children.heading: Review and comment
children.own_text: In developing the projects authorized under subparagraph (B), the Secretary shall provide for public review and comment in accordance with applicable Federal law.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Pilot projects
children.own_text: The following pilot projects are authorized for implementation, after review and approval by the Secretary, at a total cost of $69,000,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $34,500,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $34,500,000:

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: Caloosahatchee River (C-43) Basin ASR, at a total cost of $6,000,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $3,000,000 and an estimated non- Federal cost of $3,000,000.

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: Lake Belt In-Ground Reservoir Technology, at a total cost of $23,000,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $11,500,000 and an estimated non- Federal cost of $11,500,000.

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: L-31N Seepage Management, at a total cost of $10,000,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $5,000,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $5,000,000.

children.label: (iv)
children.own_text: Wastewater Reuse Technology, at a total cost of $30,000,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $15,000,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $15,000,000.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Initial projects
children.own_text: The following projects are authorized for implementation, after review and approval by the Secretary, subject to the conditions stated in subparagraph (D), at a total cost of $1,100,918,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $550,459,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $550,459,000:

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: C-44 Basin Storage Reservoir, at a total cost of $112,562,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $56,281,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $56,281,000.

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: Everglades Agricultural Area Storage Reservoirs--Phase I, at a total cost of $233,408,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $116,704,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $116,704,000.

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: Site 1 Impoundment, at a total cost of $38,535,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $19,267,500 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $19,267,500.

children.label: (iv)
children.own_text: Water Conservation Areas 3A/3B Levee Seepage Management, at a total cost of $100,335,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $50,167,500 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $50,167,500.

children.label: (v)
children.own_text: C-11 Impoundment and Stormwater Treatment Area, at a total cost of $124,837,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $62,418,500 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $62,418,500.

children.label: (vi)
children.own_text: C-9 Impoundment and Stormwater Treatment Area, at a total cost of $89,146,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $44,573,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $44,573,000.

children.label: (vii)
children.own_text: Taylor Creek/Nubbin Slough Storage and Treatment Area, at a total cost of $104,027,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $52,013,500 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $52,013,500.

children.label: (viii)
children.own_text: Raise and Bridge East Portion of Tamiami Trail and Fill Miami Canal within Water Conservation Area 3, at a total cost of $26,946,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $13,473,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $13,473,000.

children.label: (ix)
children.own_text: North New River Improvements, at a total cost of $77,087,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $38,543,500 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $38,543,500.

children.label: (x)
children.own_text: C-111 Spreader Canal, at a total cost of $94,035,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $47,017,500 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $47,017,500.

children.label: (xi)
children.own_text: Adaptive Assessment and Monitoring Program, at a total cost of $100,000,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $50,000,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $50,000,000.

children.label: (i)
children.heading: Project implementation reports
children.own_text: Before implementation of a project described in any of clauses (i) through (x) of subparagraph (C), the Secretary shall review and approve for the project a project implementation report prepared in accordance with subsections (f) and (h).

children.label: (ii)
children.heading: Submission of report
children.own_text: The Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate the project implementation report required by subsections (f) and (h) for each project under this paragraph (including all relevant data and information on all costs).

children.label: (iii)
children.heading: Funding contingent on approval
children.own_text: No appropriation shall be made to construct any project under this paragraph if the project implementation report for the project has not been approved by resolutions adopted by the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate.

children.label: (iv)
children.heading: Modified water delivery
children.own_text: No appropriation shall be made to construct the Water Conservation Area 3 Decompartmentalization and Sheetflow Enhancement Project (including component AA, Additional S-345 Structures; component QQ Phase 1, Raise and Bridge East Portion of Tamiami Trail and Fill Miami Canal within WCA 3; component QQ Phase 2, WCA 3 Decompartmentalization and Sheetflow Enhancement; and component SS, North New River Improvements) or the Central Lakebelt Storage Project (including components S and EEE, Central Lake Belt Storage Area) until the completion of the project to improve water deliveries to Everglades National Park authorized by section 104 of the Everglades National Park Protection and Expansion Act of 1989 (16 U.S.C. 410r-8).

children.label: (E)
children.heading: Maximum cost of projects
children.own_text: Section 902 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2280) shall apply to each project feature authorized under this subsection.

children.heading: In general
